publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4, build 4A102; original iPod reference and native PinePhone research
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.

record.title: Original-client pixels reached the physical panel
record.method: Source/scanout signatures, direct observation, bounded reboot and filesystem check
record.observation: The phone displayed the known color pattern and then the original client’s Connect-to-iTunes graphic. The operator also observed intermittent black frames with the backlight on.
record.limits: This establishes physical presentation of those frames. It does not establish a home screen, touch, general app rendering or flicker-free operation.

exhibits.title: The matching panel-layout control in QEMU
exhibits.alt: 720 by 1440 QEMU panel capture containing a centered, doubled setup graphic on black.
exhibits.caption: QEMU control: 720 × 1440 panel layout, with the 320 × 480 guest content centered at 2×. The physical trial has UART measurements and an operator observation; this image is not a photograph of that trial.
exhibits.interpretation: The file is reproduced unchanged. Open it at full size to inspect the capture.
exhibits.rights: Research capture; depicted Apple interface retains its original rights.

exhibits.title: Physical source and scanout receipts
exhibits.interpretation: The quoted fields are diagnostic counters/signatures, not full-frame pixel counts. The original-client frame was recorded at 52.0 s in this instrumented run; the separate visually observed run reports its client frame at 51.5 s.

exhibits.title: What the physical observation actually adds
rows: Colored quadrants, then iTunes graphic; intermittent black
UART progressed; flicker improvement not established
exhibits.interpretation: Preserving the preceding scanout during ordinary swaps is a distinct change from suppressing intentional blanking. The follow-up run cannot be promoted into visual success when it was not watched.
